mcqs.question: You're choosing a lunch: one of 4 mains AND one of 3 sides. How many total lunch combinations are there?
options: 4 (just the mains)
It depends on which main you pick
mcqs.explanation: Two independent choices combine via the product rule: 4 × 3 = 12. Adding them (7) would be the sum rule, which applies only when you're picking one option from disjoint categories, not combining independent choices.

mcqs.question: A committee needs to select 3 people from 8 to serve with no distinct roles. Which formula applies?
options: Permutation, P(8,3)
Combination, C(8,3)
8³ (repetition allowed)
8! (arrange everyone)
mcqs.explanation: Since the 3 selected people have no distinguishing roles, swapping any two of them changes nothing about the outcome — order doesn't matter, so it's a combination, C(8,3). Permutation would apply if the 3 had distinct roles (e.g. chair, secretary, treasurer).

mcqs.question: What does the pigeonhole principle actually let you conclude?
options: The exact number of items in the fullest container
That every container holds the same number of items
That at least one container must hold more than one item, without saying which
The probability that two items collide
mcqs.explanation: Pigeonhole is a pure existence argument — it guarantees a collision exists somewhere, but says nothing about where or the exact distribution. It's not a probability statement and gives no counting detail beyond 'at least one.'

mcqs.question: In the '5 points in a unit square, two are within √2/2' problem, what are the pigeonhole 'holes'?
options: The 5 points themselves
The distance value √2/2
The square's 4 corners
The 4 quadrants the square is split into
mcqs.explanation: The holes are the 4 quadrants (partitioning the square); the 5 points are the pigeons. Since 5 > 4, two points must land in the same quadrant, and that quadrant's diagonal bounds the maximum distance between them.

mcqs.question: Why does |A ∪ B| = |A| + |B| − |A ∩ B| subtract the intersection instead of just adding |A| and |B|?
options: Elements in both A and B get counted once in |A| and once in |B|, so subtracting |A∩B| removes the duplicate count
To make the formula symmetric
|A ∩ B| is always negative
It only applies when A and B don't overlap
mcqs.explanation: Any element in both sets is counted twice when you simply add |A| + |B| — once in each set's count — so subtracting the overlap exactly once corrects the count back to each such element being counted a single time.

mcqs.question: Using stars and bars, how many ways can 10 identical candies be split among 3 distinct kids (some kids may get zero)?
mcqs.explanation: Stars and bars gives C(k+n−1, n−1) = C(10+3−1, 3−1) = C(12,2) = 66. C(10,3) would undercount by ignoring repetition, and 3^10 wrongly treats the candies as distinguishable and ordered.

mcqs.question: Why isn't the number of distinct arrangements of the letters in 'BANANA' simply 6!?
options: Because 6! is always wrong for word arrangements
Because BANANA has only 5 unique letters
Because the 3 A's and 2 N's are indistinguishable from each other, so 6! overcounts by the ways to permute each repeated group internally
Because arrangement problems never use factorials
mcqs.explanation: 6! treats every letter as unique, but swapping the two N's or permuting the three A's produces the exact same visible word — dividing by 3! (for the A's) and 2! (for the N's) removes those invisible duplicate counts, giving the correct 60.
